Deleted both byte-identical repositoryRefFromPatch copies from internal/ingest/processor.go and internal/revieworder/service.go; both call sites are now one line. 'strings' dropped from processor.go as it became unused.

Fixed: deleted AGENTS.md:1-40 (the hand-written duplicate that said 'bd sync' and '--status in_progress'), leaving the hash-stamped BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION block as the single source of truth, with a short header explaining why it must not be restated. Fixed: docs/security-review.md:113 and :130 now say 'security/audit/progress notifications on kind 25910', matching the wording already at nostr-protocol.md:113, instead of prescribing the retired NIP-90 kind 7000.

Duplicate. Fixed: new internal/gitexec (Command/Harden/Run/RunBytes/WaitError) carries the hardened env (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0) and stderr extraction that previously existed only in workspacesnapshot.runGitBytes. All six forks migrated; repo.Manager's streaming variants build on Command+WaitError with the four Kill/Wait copies folded into killAndWait. Scope extended to git clone and the three git apply sites (same credential-prompt hazard, same file) and the dead runGitStdout fork deleted. Review correction applied: WaitError originally rendered with %s, dropping the *exec.ExitError; it now wraps via an Unwrap-ing error type so exit codes stay recoverable, with a regression test that fails against the %s version. Verified the four exit-code-sensitive call sites (codemap/graph.go:167,183,191 and contextbuilder/search.go:160) deliberately keep their own exec.Cmd for git grep's ExitCode()==1 no-match handling.

Fixed: go-gitdiff (already a direct dependency, already used for this in contextbuilder) replaces the hand-rolled parser in scanner.go (ParseDiffAddedLines, parseHunkNewStart deleted) and provider.go (extractChangedFiles). Both documented bugs covered by tests verified failing against the old parser first: TestParseDiffAddedLines_NoNewlineAtEOFDoesNotDrift (old parser reported adds at {2,3} instead of {1,2}) and TestParseDiffAddedLines_NoPrefix (old parser returned empty). Follow-on found during Item 4 and fixed here: the swap had preserved the SILENT-failure shape — a parse error returned an empty result, so ScanFiles skipped every file and betterleaks filtered out every secret with no error. 29 of 31 heldout corpus patches trigger this. Parse errors now propagate; ScanFiles returns (ScanResult, error); decision-path callers (pipeline, securityreview, betterleaks, auditengine) surface it as a hard error while the advisory context-layer path degrades to a LayerWarning. Invariant test added: unparseable diff must error, never read as a clean scan.

Fixed: findingKey (the 5-line quantised bucket with the 4|5 boundary defect) deleted; one exported reviewengine.SameFindingLocus (file+category case-insensitive, within 2 lines) is now the single identity predicate shared by mergeFindings, DeduplicateFindings and securityscan.MergeScannerFindings. The three copies of the drop-the-error normalize pattern now propagate. securityscan.DeduplicateFindings renamed MergeScannerFindings, matching its own doc comment. Two over-reaches caught in review and reverted: the agent had switched the scanner-LLM representative to highest-confidence (which, since scanner.go:186 stamps a flat 1.0 on every regex hit including hedged rules, would have buried LLM explanations under terse rule text) and dropped the +0.15 corroboration boost — fx05 was about identity, not merge policy, so both were restored. A final pre-commit review then caught a regression the unification introduced: clustering compared against the cluster's moving representative, so findings chained transitively (lines 1/3/5 collapsing into one cluster where the old bucket rule gave two) and results depended on confidence ordering. Fixed with a stable per-cluster Anchor. Fixed in passing: cluster.Models appended per finding rather than per distinct route, so one model reporting two nearby findings satisfied RequireConsensus on its own. Three tests added, all verified failing against the buggy code.

Fixed: new internal/safepath (Normalize, RejectSymlinkComponents) replaces the line-for-line duplicate confinement logic. workspacesnapshot aliases its ErrInvalidPath/ErrOutsideScope/ErrSymlink sentinels to safepath's so errors.Is identity is preserved; contextbuilder delegates and maps back to its single ErrUnsafeRepositoryPath, keeping the fs.ErrNotExist passthrough in validateRepositoryPaths. Independent review confirmed the confinement rules (symlink resolution, .. handling, absolute-path and NUL rejection, dot handling) match both prior implementations. Note: the audit had recorded a dependency on DRYDOCK-js0a; that was backwards — js0a (rejecting symlinked snapshot storage roots) is separate follow-up work that this consolidation makes easier, not a blocker. Dependency removed.

Fixed: deleted the answer-key mock (reviewerCandidates/verifiedCandidates/confusionCounts and the FakeLLM+securityverify scaffolding) from both harnesses. The security harness now runs securityscan.New().ScanFiles over the held-out corpus and scores via the canonical eval.Harness.RunMonthly metric, removing the duplicated and non-matching TP/FP/FN math. Honest result recorded rather than tuned: precision 1.000, recall 0.286 (tp=4, fp=0, fn=10) — the regex scanner catches exactly the 4 regex-detectable classes and flags none of the 6 clean cases; floors set at recall >= 0.25 and precision >= 0.75 so any single-rule regression fails. The Nostr harness now runs the exact auditengine wiring (NewWithRuleSets(PresenceRulesForRoles, SurfaceRules).ScanFiles + LocateSurface + AnalyzeAbsences) and asserts per-rule vulnerable-flags/fixed-clears. Duplicate eval/testdata/nostr-detector.golden.json deleted. Two discoveries filed rather than papered over: DRYDOCK-dfl3 (29 of 31 corpus patches have malformed hunk headers — this is what exposed the silent-scan bug now fixed under DRYDOCK-xfan) and DRYDOCK-09c1 (absence rules V1/V5/V7/R1/R2 and the relay fixture are not exercised by this corpus; no fake assertion was added for them).

Fixed: docker/lsp-bridge/Dockerfile now mirrors the root Dockerfile's hardening. Non-root via useradd --uid 1000 drydock + USER drydock, so the bridge and every language server it spawns against attacker-supplied repo contents run unprivileged. Single Go toolchain: COPY --from=builder /usr/local/go replaces the separate go1.23.6 runtime download, so gopls is built by the same 1.26 toolchain that parses the modules it serves. All versions pinned via ARG (gopls v0.23.0, Node 20.19.4 from a pinned tarball which also removes the curl-pipe-to-root-shell, typescript 5.7.3, typescript-language-server 6.0.0, python-lsp-server 1.15.0, rust-analyzer 2026-08-24), matching how the core Dockerfile pins BETTERLEAKS_VERSION. The two UTF-8 replacement characters on line 1 restored to an em-dash. NOT BUILT — the image is multi-GB; reviewed by reading only. The Go-toolchain-copy from an alpine builder into an ubuntu runtime is the one step that would fail at build time if wrong, which is a loud failure rather than a silent one.

Fixed: extracted four seams from pipeline.Runner.process following the pattern already established in the file (tryAutoFix, checkReviewStatus, publishApplyFailure, indexSourceCode were all previously pulled from this same function): authorizePayment, buildReviewContext, publishExclusionOnlyReview, runReview. process went from ~609 to 478 lines. Both hazards handled deliberately: the releasePrepared closure, its defer and the explicit pre-meta-review call stay in process so the lease frees on every return path (buildReviewContext returns prepared but does not own release), and the timer.Time wrappers stay in process so stage tracing and the durable MarkReviewPaymentBlocked side effect fire at the same points. Added a direct test of the previously-untestable authorizePayment seam covering terminal denial (persists the block, stops after one attempt), the allowed path, and payment_pending using the ordinary requeue without persisting a terminal block. Independent pre-commit review confirmed control flow, early returns and error propagation are equivalent to the inlined code. The optional metareview failureStage fold-in was declined with reasons: failureStage is persisted to the audit row and drives MetaReviewFailures metrics, which tracing.PipelineTimer.Time does not write, so a faithful refactor would need a new stage-wrapping closure — correctly judged against the no-new-wrappers rule rather than forced.

Fixed: every bare unwrapped driver return in internal/db (store_payments.go, store_marketplace.go, store_codechat.go, store.go) and internal/reviewsession/store.go now wraps with fmt.Errorf("verb noun: %w", err), matching the house style in store_monitoring.go / store_idegateway.go / store_review_orders.go. store_marketplace.go:144 now wraps sql.ErrNoRows instead of returning a bare formatted string. reviewsession lookup scans route through the package's existing mapNotFound helper. The six discarded json.Marshal/Unmarshal errors on persisted reviewer-profile columns now propagate — previously a malformed languages column yielded a silently-empty slice and the reviewer stopped matching any language with nothing logged. Returns that propagate already-wrapped inner errors were deliberately left bare (store_security.go 256/301/430 and equivalents). A nil-wrap regression introduced mid-work (unconditional wrap turning a nil error into a non-nil %!w(<nil>)) was caught by the db tests, fixed, and the five files swept for other instances. Independent pre-commit review confirmed no unconditional wrap of a possibly-nil error remains and that the db.Err* sentinels consumed via errors.Is in codechat/conversation handlers are unaffected.

Fixed as part of the DRYDOCK-fx05 review cycle. mergedFinding gained a stable Anchor field set once at cluster creation; membership is decided against the anchor rather than the moving representative, so clustering no longer chains transitively (lines 1/3/5 now give two clusters, matching the old exact-bucket rule) and no longer depends on confidence ordering. The higher-confidence finding still becomes the representative for explanatory fields. Separately, cluster.Models now appends each route only once via containsRoute, so one model reporting two nearby findings can no longer satisfy RequireConsensus or earn the consensus boost on its own — a pre-existing bug the widened window made materially more likely. Three tests added (TestSameFindingLocus, TestMergeFindings_StableAnchorNoChaining, TestMergeFindings_ConsensusNotSatisfiedBySingleRoute); the two behavioural ones were verified failing against the buggy code. TestSameFindingLocus also restores the finding-identity coverage lost when TestFindingKey was deleted with the old bucket key.

Fixed: auditReviewInstructions now takes the depth budget, caps candidate files to MaxUnits and scopes surface locations to those files, so the prompt payload is bounded by the same discipline the engine already applies to units. Regression test verified failing against the unbounded version.

Fixed: the three SCA tools now run with --format sarif and parseSARIFFindings decodes runs[].results[] into typed structs, so path and message come from the same object. Deleted parseExternalFindings/walkJSON/firstString/firstInt. Pre-commit review then caught that the initial SARIF severity mapping (error->high, warning->medium, default->low) silently downgraded every trivy/grype/osv CRITICAL to high, losing P0; severity now resolves result properties.severity, then security-severity CVSS, then rule properties, then the level mapping, and an absent level maps to warning per the SARIF 2.1.0 default rather than low.

Fixed: reviewengine.Finding gained RuleID and CWE fields; deterministic findings populate them with clean Evidence. auditengine.findingCWE is now a field read, the reviewUnits re-prefix block is gone, and nostrprobe.Corroborate matches on RuleID instead of an Evidence substring. The agent caught that this would have silently broken securityverify.nostrRuleID (which detected Nostr findings by scanning prose) and killed the Nostr refute lens with no failing test; minimal fix plus regression test. Pre-commit review queried whether RuleID survives the verifier round-trip — investigated and disproved: securityverify overwrites only Category/Severity/Confidence/Suggestion on a by-value copy, so RuleID travels untouched. TestRunPreservesRuleIDThroughVerification locks that invariant.

Fixed: every vulnerability in knowledge/pack.v1.json gained a validated cwe field; securityscan.RuleCWE resolves SEC-* from the map and NOSTR-* from the pack, and nostrprobe.cweForRule reads the pack. Resolves the measured divergences where the same rule reached SARIF with a different CWE depending on whether the static or dynamic path produced it. docs/nostr-security-review.md reconciled to the pack (V1 345, V7 345, R2 20).

Fixed: one nostrscan.Activate replaces the near-verbatim duplicate in securityreview/stage.go and auditengine/engine.go; deleted effectiveNostrRoles/filterNostrRules/filterNostrFindings/nostrReviewFindings and their auditNostr* twins. Resolves the named drift: the PR path now filters findings to changed files and scopes absence analysis to changed-file surfaces instead of sweeping the full repo inside a patch review.

Partially fixed — the security-relevant half. securityscan.Rule gained a Confidence field (HeuristicRuleConfidence = 0.5) and SEC-010/011/030/060, whose own descriptions say Possible/may enable, now carry it; dedup.go only lets a scanner finding boost or upgrade a colliding LLM finding when it is itself high-confidence. Pre-commit review caught that the gate was applied to the non-sensitive branch only, so a hedged sensitive finding still upgraded severity; mergeSensitiveFinding is now gated too, with a table test covering hedged/literal/legacy-zero confidences. The severity VOCABULARY consolidation is deliberately NOT done and is not being tracked as a gap: reviewengine cannot import securityscan (securityscan already imports reviewengine, so it would cycle), the natural homes both invert a dependency, and the only clean alternative is a new leaf package — larger than the typo-safety it would buy.

Fixed: the four overmatching *UseNameRE, whose discriminating suffix sat in an optional group so the rule reduced to contains-one-of-these-verbs, are now named verb slices plus a strings.Contains check. v1UseNameRE kept — its suffixes are genuinely required. Behaviour-preserving; it stops advertising precision it never had. displayName/processRequest/budgetCheck no longer masquerade as high and critical findings.

Fixed: the forged-event kludge is gone. HandleAcceptance/HandleRejection split into thin decoders calling typed recordAcceptance/recordRejection, mirroring the existing HandleCompletion->complete pattern, so the ContextVM handlers use the ParamsAs result directly instead of mutating req.Event's Content and PubKey and re-unmarshalling. Added shared verifySignedIntent and applied it to acceptance, rejection AND completion. DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE on an authorization path: acceptance and rejection now verify the envelope signature, which they previously did not while completion did — that asymmetry was the kludge's doing. Pre-commit review then caught that the exported HandleAcceptance/HandleRejection had become test-only and still unverified, so the authorization tests were exercising a path production no longer takes; both were deleted and their tests retargeted at the live ContextVM path. TestContextVMAcceptanceRejectsForgedEnvelope verified failing against pre-fix.

Fixed: one contextvm.ValidateEnvelope(req, EnvelopePolicy{...ExpirationRequired}) replaces the hand-rolled p-tag/method/e-tag/expiration blocks in revieworder (ExpirationRequired: true) and marketplace feedback (false) — the one intentional per-method difference is now an explicit flag rather than a separate implementation. idegateway.validateRequestEnvelope deliberately NOT migrated: it is a genuinely different shape (session/request binding, no expiration, intentionally omits sender/ID checks, tests use unsigned zero-value events) and is reached only through ingest, which authenticates. Tests added for addressing and the required-vs-optional replay policy.

Fixed: revieworder.reviewOrderRPCError exported as revieworder.RPCError and idegateway.processPatchReviewRequest now delegates to it. DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: an IDE-path rate limit now returns -32005 RateLimited instead of -32603 Internal, and a payment denial -32006 PaymentRequired with the retryable/reason data payload preserved instead of -32001 Unauthorized with the payload lost. Clients can now distinguish retryable from payable through both doors.

Fixed: Signer declared once in internal/signing, RelayPublisher once in internal/publisher; the duplicate declarations removed from contextvm, marketplace, idegateway, profile, conversation, codechat and publisher's own local copy. codechat.Keyer now embeds signing.Signer + Encrypt, and its Decrypt was dropped (zero callers) with decryptDM renamed dmPlaintext — it validated a rumor kind and returned content verbatim, so the name asserted a confidentiality property the function did not provide. The related interface duplications were folded in by Item D: ToolRunner deduped to nostrprobe.ToolRunner, PaymentAuthorizer to payment.PatchAuthorizer, MonitoringRegistry to monitoring.Membership.

Fixed: facades.go reduced 151 -> 13 lines, keeping only the policy-owning PatchFacade; the eight free functions and five empty stateless facade structs are gone, and each provider's Build now calls its internal analyze*Content directly. audit_facades.go deliberately kept — those facades own real policy (closed name sets, input validation, warning normalization). The bare *LayerWarning type assertion is gone by deletion; the production path already used errors.As. The tautological f(x)==f(x) test deleted and its real coverage (empty-input behaviour) retargeted at the production providers.

Fixed: LoopRunner.Run is now the single agent tool loop, with LoopRequest extended by TerminalTool/TerminalStop/Finalize, an empty-assistant policy, and OnMessage/OnToolResult hooks; ExecuteReviewer's ~150-line hand-rolled copy is replaced by a Run call mapping LoopTrace to ReviewerTrace via the existing reviewerTrace(). Both named drifts resolved: per-message PromptTokens/CompletionTokens are now populated on the selection path too, and discovery nudges once on a tool-less turn instead of burning a turn re-sending an identical request. Discovery deliberately does not hard-fail on an empty assistant turn — its exhaustion-to-deterministic-fallback contract requires reaching ErrTurnLimit. Pre-commit review confirmed stop reasons, turn/tool budgets, cancellation classification and ErrReviewSubmitMissing wrapping are preserved for both former callers.

Fixed: deleted ~250 lines — extractMetaReviewJSON, repairInvalidJSONEscapes and the whole parseFlexible*/flexibleItems coercion bank. parseMetaReviewOutput now uses llmutil.ExtractJSON plus strict json.Unmarshal plus Validate, and the completion routes through the newly exported reviewengine.CompleteStructured, which sets JSONMode and runs the schema-hint repair loop. A model producing wrong-typed output is now re-prompted rather than silently coerced and graded as if it complied. The two slop-ratifying tests (coercion tolerance, escape repair) replaced with a strict-rejection guard verified failing against the tolerant parser.

Fixed: the 29-line randomized BFS over map[string]any replaced by a fixed-path typed decode of .Review — the path was always fixed because turn.Result is always json.Marshal(RunOutput). Removes the only map[string]any escape hatch in the package and makes CompactHistory's documented determinism true rather than aspirational. All five test fixtures corrected from the capitalised shape production never emits to the real lowercase one, which is why the implementation had been widened to accept both. Two guards added: one exercising json.Marshal(RunOutput) directly (zero prior coverage) and one proving a decoy sibling with colliding keys never wins — the decoy guard verified failing against the BFS. Findings deliberately kept as json.RawMessage rather than decoded into ReviewerOutput: the typed round-trip re-marshals every zero-valued field and inflates the compacted output past its budget.

Fixed: one (m *Manager) runGitApply(ctx, repoPath, patch, flags...) holds applySinglePatch's already-correct stdin handling (write error via channel, ctx.Done() guard, wrapped open-stdin error, ErrClosedPipe ignored); the three callers are 1-3 lines with their flag sets unchanged (--3way --index, --check, --index). Both silent-drop copies — which never even ASSIGNED io.WriteString's error — are gone, so a failed pipe write now surfaces as 'write patch content:' instead of masquerading as 'does not apply cleanly' and silently dropping a valid autofix. Net -56 lines. Honest caveat from the implementer: the specific silent write-error is not deterministically unit-testable because git apply reads all of stdin before exiting 0, and no injection seam exists that would not itself be slop; the existing autofix apply/check/skip tests pass and prove behaviour is preserved. Pre-commit review independently confirmed flag sets and write-error propagation.

Fixed: the three parallel model-endpoint enumerations collapsed into one modelEndpoints() table ranged at all three sites (reachability warnings, production requireExplicit/requireLLMAPIKey, and the new requireTLSEndpoint). Sec70B*, SecClassify*, SecLocalize* and AgenticDiscovery* now get the production TLS/loopback guard, closing the hole where DRYDOCK_SEC70B_BASE_URL=http://... passed validation silently while main.go sent the GLOBAL DRYDOCK_LLM_API_KEY to it in plaintext. DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: in production an http/loopback URL for any sec or agentic-discovery endpoint is now a hard error; optional endpoints left empty stay optional. TestValidateProductionGuardsSecurityEndpointTLS fails 4/4 against pre-fix. Pre-commit review confirmed the table is complete against the nine endpoints main.go constructs and that no endpoint lost a check it previously had; a test that optional-and-empty endpoints produce no error was added on review.

Fixed together with okwr, since they shared a root cause. normalizeStream now checks ctx.Err() on channel close for a deterministic cancellation-vs-completion decision, routes every send through a prefer-send-then-ctx.Done() trySend, and uses a buffered(1) out channel so the terminal event is deposited deterministically and a consumer that cancels cannot pin the goroutine. Passes 300 consecutive runs and -race -count=50; previously reproduced reliably under -count=200 (and at HEAD, confirming it was pre-existing rather than introduced). Pre-commit review confirmed the terminal-event-exactly-once contract holds on every exit path and no event can be dropped or duplicated.

Partially fixed. The lossy streaming round-trip is closed: the streaming adapter now carries the terminal Result.Content/Usage and normalizeStream uses terminal content when no deltas accumulated, so a provider returning full text in the terminal Result.Content — the documented shape — no longer yields an empty string. TestStreamCompletionUsesTerminalResultContent yields the empty value pre-fix and full text post-fix. The cancellation race is fixed under DRYDOCK-1sly. For parity, added TestPublicTypesMirrorInternalFields (reflect-based field parity) in pkg/codemap. Two deliberate declines: unkeyed-literal parity guards are rejected by go vet (confirmed empirically), and enum type-aliasing would leak internal types into the public SDK, against that package's stated purpose.

Fixed: recomputed and rewrote 30 malformed hunk-header counts in eval/heldout-sample.json from each hunk body, preserving start offsets. Verified by the orchestrator: only patch_diff changed, in 30 of 31 cases; case_id, changed_files, context_bundle and expected_findings are untouched in all 31, and every hunk header is now internally consistent with its body. All 31 patches parse with go-gitdiff, so the harness dropped its tolerant-walk workaround and scannerRunner now exercises the real diff-aware path instead of passing an empty diff. Metrics unchanged and honest: precision 1.000, recall 0.286.

Fixed (remaining items; 1/6/7/10 were already done in phase 1). Deleted .env.lemmy and its deployment.md section — it was a drifted subset of .env.example, already missing seven variables. Removed the TARGETARCH/GOARCH cross-compile no-op from the root Dockerfile. Collapsed entrypoint.sh to 'listener|drift-guard) exec ... $@' so the listener arm no longer silently discards its arguments. Corrected docs/configuration.md's DRYDOCK_MODE row, which asserted the opposite of the code (main.go does read it) and omitted drift-guard. Deleted the unreachable env-fallback and splitTokenList in lspbridge/server/handler.go — the auth surface where the answer depended on which dead code path you read — and configuredLSPCommandConfigs plus its helpers, ~55 lines reachable only from t.Setenv.

Fixed: exported codemap.CacheVersion, codemap.ResolveCacheDir and codemap.WriteJSONAtomic; nostrscan now shares all three, dropping its own cacheVersion constant, its duplicate cache-dir git logic and its ~30-line inline atomic temp-writer. Added gitexec.Output (Run + TrimSpace) replacing three identical gitOutput wrappers in codemap/nostrscan/auditengine. TestCacheSharesCodemapDirAndVersion locks the linkage that a version bump must now invalidate both packages' entries — previously each defined its own cacheVersion = 1 while writing into the same drydock-codemap directory, so bumping one left the other's stale entries live. Deliberately NOT merged: gitBlob (nostrscan is size-capped streaming via StdoutPipe/LimitReader, codemap is a plain RunBytes) and tree-listing (different path filters and struct types) — genuinely different semantics, not forks.

Closed: all four pre-commit review defects resolved, and one of the four turned out not to be a defect. (1) securityscan/dedup.go — the >=0.8 corroboration gate was applied to the non-sensitive branch only, so a hedged SENSITIVE finding still boosted confidence and upgraded severity; mergeSensitiveFinding is now gated too, with a table test over hedged/literal/legacy-zero confidences. (2) auditengine sarifSeverity silently downgraded every trivy/grype/osv CRITICAL to high (SARIF has no level above error), losing P0; severity now resolves result properties.severity, then security-severity CVSS, then rule properties, then the level mapping, and an absent level maps to warning per the spec default rather than low. (3) The claim that Finding.RuleID would be dropped across the securityverify round-trip was investigated and DISPROVED — securityverify overwrites only Category/Severity/Confidence/Suggestion on a by-value copy, so RuleID travels untouched; TestRunPreservesRuleIDThroughVerification added to lock that invariant if a future change ever reconstructs findings from the model response. (4) The exported marketplace HandleAcceptance/HandleRejection had become test-only while still trusting event.PubKey with no CheckID/VerifySignature, so the authorization tests exercised a path production no longer takes; both deleted and the tests retargeted at the live ContextVM path. Separately, the review's claim that the prefix-512 isProbablyText change could blow up the context bundle was checked and is a false positive — providers.go checks out.Len() before writing and truncates to 4KB first.
Already fixed in the phase-1 review cycle (stable per-cluster Anchor plus distinct-route consensus counting); this duplicate tracking entry is closed. See the DRYDOCK-fx05 close note for detail.
Split by package into DRYDOCK-2sgt/9iqd/0fcn/txra/ll1m/uf9b/jyjm/lxh5; 10 entries fixed this session, ~3 verified stale. See notes.

All items complete: db-hygiene items (4/6/7) and tautological-test deletions (1/3/5/8/9/10) done in earlier phases; git-fixture + golden helper consolidation (item 11) done in Item 4 via internal/testutil.
Authored eval fixtures that genuinely trigger V1/V5/V7/R1/R2 + the relay fixture through production wiring; TestNostrProductionWiringFlagsVulnerableFixtures green.

Fixed: Restore now calls safepath.RejectSymlinkComponents on the snapshot directory, descriptor.json, patch and (for mutable copies) the files root, each BEFORE the corresponding read — rejecting a symlinked storage dir, symlinked descriptor/patch entries, a symlinked files root and component swaps under the trusted root. Snapshot.Resolve now Lstats filesRoot itself, closing the 'rejects symlinks below filesRoot but never the root' gap on the mutable read path. Manifest/hash verification untouched, per the acceptance criteria: the existing tamper->ErrHashMismatch test and a new clean-restore subcase both still pass. TestRestoreRejectsSymlinkedStorage (5 subcases) and TestMutableReadRejectsSymlinkedFilesRoot verified failing against pre-fix. Note this issue predated internal/safepath (extracted in phase 1) — that primitive was reused rather than writing a third confinement implementation.

Fixed: the audit engine's Dependencies.CodeMap is now codemap.New(codemap.WithLSPClient(lspClient)), and internal/securityreview gained WithLSPClient wired from main.go so the PR security lens uses the type-aware code map too — both halves, not just the audit path the issue prescribed. Both degrade to the grep path when the sidecar is absent, so the audit never depends on it. Caught a latent production panic while doing it: WithLSPClient stored a typed-nil *lspbridge.Client in the interface, so passing the legitimately-nil client would make b.lsp != nil true and panic on the first Analyze; it is now nil-safe. Also applied the honesty half, which matters independently of LSP: absence evidence now reads 'reference path:' rather than formatting as a proven call path, because a grep-derived edge can come from a comment or a string literal. TestAbsenceEvidenceLabelsReferencePathNotCall verified failing pre-fix.

Fixed. Both review outbox trios collapsed to one reviewOutbox{table, keyCols, noun} with byte-equivalent SQL (column order, ON CONFLICT keys, deliveredAt > 0) and error text preserved verbatim via noun; the six public Store methods are now one-line bindings. The security-audit outbox was deliberately left separate after inspection — it reserves a 3-publication set plus a SARIF artifact atomically inside a state-validated transaction, a genuinely different shape that would fit the helper badly; same conclusion the previous phase reached. New store_outbox_test.go pins the guarantee this mechanism exists for — reserving twice with a different event for the same key returns the FIRST event's ID — across both key shapes; that had zero db-level coverage before. Four further genuine SELECT+Scan duplications collapsed following the scanReviewOrder precedent: ReviewTask (3 copies), ReviewerProfile, assignment list rows, PromptVersion. Write/aggregate 'pairs' correctly judged not-genuine and skipped. db.RowQuerier exported and now used by both the store_payments anonymous interface and reviewsession.sqlQuerier. UpsertSubscription left untouched (money path, owner decision).

Stage 2a landed: dep-runner sidecar (internal/deprunner client+server, cmd/dep-runner, docker/dep-runner/Dockerfile, compose depupgrade profile) plus UpgradesConfig with operator-only allow_scripts rejection. Architecture: sidecar over HTTP+bearer token following the lsp-bridge precedent, NOT a Docker socket mount — socket access is effectively host root and would have been granted to the service that executes untrusted repository content. Residual risk stated: successive requests share one container's kernel/PID namespace. Stage 5 landed — the dependency-upgrade feature is now wired end to end and ships operator-disabled.
Head-change detection: repository_snapshots gains head_commit (schemaSQL for fresh DBs plus guarded versioned migration v15 for existing ones); UpsertRepositorySnapshot is a compare-then-write in a transaction returning SnapshotUpsert{RepoID, HeadChanged, NewHead}. HeadChanged is true only when the write actually applied (respecting the existing created_at guard), the new head is non-empty, and it differs — so out-of-order/older events never trigger, and first observation scans once. Only one caller existed, so blast radius was small.
Wiring: ingest gains an optional DependencyUpgrader + WithDependencyUpgrades; depupgrade/trigger.go adds a bounded queue with N workers, monitoring-gated non-blocking enqueue, RunScheduled, and reconcile. Operator knobs DRYDOCK_DEPUPGRADE_ENABLED/INTERVAL/WORKERS with Validate rules (interval>0, workers>=1, and when enabled DEP_RUNNER_URL + MONITORED_REPOS_AUTHOR required); in-process ticker in the composition root mirroring runReviewLifecycle, fail-closed hard-exit on misconfig.
Four decisions, all with reasons: schedule is an in-process ticker and triggers.schedule is a BOOLEAN opt-in rather than a cadence token, because per-repo cadence would be a false promise against one shared ticker without new persistence or a wasted clone per sweep; new_patch was DROPPED (and its enum value removed) because cheap manifest pre-detection only works for kind-1617 — 1618 has no diff pre-preparation — so the knob would silently no-op for half the kinds; non-local go.mod replace directives are REFUSED via x/mod/modfile before anything reaches the sidecar, as a VCS-fetch/egress vector on untrusted input, skipping without writing state so it re-evaluates if the repo drops the replace; reconciliation re-queries root NIP-34 status on each sweep to mark merged/rejected, avoiding a second ingest notification path.
AutoOnSnapshot: resolved as a documented DEPRECATION SHIM, not deleted. The first pass deleted it, which was what I asked for, but that was my error: KnownFields(true) turns a stale key into a decode error and the hot callers (pipeline/runner.go:382, revieworder/service.go:303) respond by discarding the ENTIRE repo config and falling back to Default() with only a Warn — so deleting it would silently downgrade a live repository's whole gating/review/ignore policy, which is strictly worse than a dead knob. The field is now accepted, read by nothing, documented as such, with a test pinning that a config carrying the key still parses AND retains its other non-default settings.
